Question Choices: A fair spinner is labeled 1 through 10. Given that the result is prime, what is the probability that it is greater than 5?
Hints: The prime outcomes are 2, 3, 5, and 7;Only one of those outcomes is greater than 5
Solution: Conditioning on a prime result leaves $\{2,3,5,7\}$.;Only $7$ is greater than $5$, so the probability is $1/4$.

Question Choices: Two distinguishable fair dice are rolled. Given that their sum is 7, what is the probability that the first die is even?
Hints: List the six ordered outcomes whose sum is 7;The first die is even in three of them
Solution: The reduced sample space is $\{(1,6),(2,5),(3,4),(4,3),(5,2),(6,1)\}$.;The first die is even in $3$ of the $6$ outcomes, so the probability is $1/2$.

Question Choices: A 4-person committee is chosen uniformly from 10 students. Given that Lina is selected, what is the probability that Omar is also selected?
Hints: With Lina fixed, 3 of the remaining 9 students will be selected;Use the probability that Omar occupies one of those 3 places
Solution: After Lina is fixed, the committee has $3$ open places among $9$ students.;Omar is selected with probability $3/9=1/3$.

Question Choices: One card is drawn from a standard deck. Given that it is black, what is the probability that it is a queen?
Hints: There are 26 black cards;Two queens are black;Use black queens over black cards
Solution: The condition leaves $26$ black cards.;The queen of clubs and queen of spades are favorable, so the probability is $2/26=1/13$.

Question Choices: Three students are chosen uniformly from 7 students, including Alex, Blair, and Casey. Given that Alex and Blair are both selected, what is the probability that Casey is also selected?
Hints: Alex and Blair already occupy two places;The third member is chosen from the remaining 5 students;Only Casey is favorable
Solution: With Alex and Blair fixed, the last committee member is equally likely to be any of the remaining $5$ students.;Therefore Casey is selected with probability $1/5$.
